reference_knowledge.evidence: Source-linked specifications and scopes; profile estimates must not be confused with measured emulsion properties.
reference_knowledge.coverage: Displayed stock inventory; detailed per-stock colour profiles pending audit. Reviewed in docs/film-color-science.md; its six-axis overlay values are deliberately not stored, because the site labels them uncalibrated.

reference_knowledge.evidence: Exposure, development, and output medium jointly shape the rendering. RGB cannot uniquely recover a scene spectrum.
reference_knowledge.coverage: Bundled stock names and types, plus print media named in its README, names only; synthetic examples excluded. No engine code or spectral datasets copied.

reference_knowledge.evidence: Five-level appearance ratings are subjective descriptions, not calibrated physical measurements.
reference_knowledge.coverage: 66 named stock records in embedded data (page counter states 50); factual ordinal ratings only, no article prose or photographs copied.

reference_knowledge.evidence: Development and output choices can outweigh stock differences; one scan does not isolate an emulsion.
reference_knowledge.coverage: Curated methodological caution, plus specific stocks named in the article, names only.

reference_knowledge.local_path: assets/docs/The ultimate guide to Fuji’s Film Simulations; A DEEP dive to de-mystify one of Fuji’s best features.html
reference_knowledge.evidence: Film simulation uses selective hue, saturation and tone mappings; presets are not physical emulsions.
reference_knowledge.coverage: 12 simulation families in the supplied 2020 guide. Filter variants are modifiers, not new emulsions.

reference_knowledge.evidence: Histogram display and endpoint clipping are separate from inferred scene exposure.
reference_knowledge.coverage: UI inspiration only: channel histograms, exact counts, clipping readouts; no source code copied.

reference_knowledge.title: Every 35mm Film Color Science Explained, Part 1
reference_knowledge.evidence: One controlled chart test per film under a single workflow; raw patch values and the saturation formula are unpublished.
reference_knowledge.coverage: Own-words summaries of 14 films in film_color_notes.json. No transcript, frames or preset data are stored.

film_look_notes.title: Analogue Shop film stock samples
film_look_notes.evidence: A retailer's general descriptions, written to sell film. No lab, developer, scanner or exposure is stated.
film_look_notes.coverage: Own-words summaries of the written descriptions on 26 stock pages that match a catalog direction. No photographs, captions or credits are stored or were used.
film_look_notes.limits: The sample photographs belong to third-party photographers, with no licence stated, so they are not reference material. The Cinestill 50D page links to a differently named product, and the Cinestill 800T description sits at a URL naming another film.

film_look_notes.title: Kodak Film Guide (Josh Solomon, Casual Photophile, 2018)
film_look_notes.evidence: One writer's opinions from 2018. The article states no method, lab or scanner.
film_look_notes.coverage: Own-words summaries of its 14 Kodak films, 12 of them catalog directions. Its statements about availability are not stored, as they date from 2018. No article text or photographs are stored.
film_look_notes.limits: Comparisons between films are the writer's. Pro Image 100 and Double X are context only, as they are not catalog directions.

film_color_notes.title: Every 35mm Film Color Science Explained, Part 1 (PARVEC)
film_color_notes.method: A SpyderCHECKR 24 chart under a controlled high-CRI lamp, with one camera and lens, lab development, camera scanning, and greyscale normalisation by linear stretch at 10% and 90%, then read on a vectorscope.
film_color_notes.limits: One workflow, usually one roll, 35mm. Raw patch values and the saturation formula are unpublished, and the signs of some reported figures are unresolved. Film Color Reference (filmreference.ron.nyc) audits these claims and labels them low confidence. Notes are FilmLook's own summaries, not measurements, and the preset data is not used.

records.name: ACROS
records.description: Monochrome rendering with brightness-dependent texture; optional colour filters.

records.name: ASTIA/Soft
records.description: Gentler portrait rendering with selective hue and saturation changes.

records.name: Candido 800T
records.notes: Tungsten-balanced, based on a motion-picture stock. In daylight, greens, blues and violets shift toward cyan, and reds intensify toward orange. Red halation around highlights and among the least accurate. The results do not automatically transfer to CineStill 800T.

records.look: Natural and slightly warm, softly cinematic rather than saturated. Controlled contrast with gentle gradation at both ends, and extremely fine grain. Wants strong daylight.

records.name: CineStill 50D
records.palette: Two opposing axes, blue to gold and cyan to orange
records.notes: Greens to yellows and violets to magentas lose saturation, while blues and cyans keep it. Reds drift to a soft, pale orange, so skin looks muted against cool backgrounds. Red glow around bright areas, from the removed antihalation layer. Low colour accuracy; strongest at golden and blue hour.

records.look: Cool, cinematic, richly contrasted, with obvious halation around light sources. For night, city and tungsten-lit interiors.

records.name: CineStill-like
records.character: Tungsten-balanced motion-picture character: cool shadows, glowing warm practical lights, visible halation around point sources.
records.suits: Night streets, neon, tungsten interiors, mixed artificial light.
records.poor_fit: Flat midday daylight and scenes with no bright practical lights.

records.name: CLASSIC CHROME
records.description: Restrained saturation and documentary colour relationships.

records.name: Classic Neg.
records.description: Colour-negative-inspired rendering with tone-dependent colour shifts.

records.look: A motion-picture black-and-white film. Gritty and stark, with high contrast that crushes shadows and blows highlights, though midtones are smooth under controlled light. Not for novices.

records.name: ETERNA Bleach Bypass
records.description: Reduced colour saturation with stronger tonal contrast.

records.name: ETERNA/Cinema
records.description: Restrained cinematic saturation and soft tonal contrast.

records.look: Moderate contrast with soft transitions, and visible but not dominant grain. Slightly vintage and less clinical. For daylight and moderate light.

records.name: Fujifilm 200
records.notes: Its scope sat almost on top of ColorPlus 200, with slightly less yellow greens. The author infers a Kodak-made stock; neither company has confirmed it, and Film Color Reference does not treat it as an identity.

records.name: Pro 400H-like
records.character: Airy pastel negative: soft cool-leaning greens and blues, luminous overexposed highlights, gentle contrast.
records.suits: Foliage, overcast or open-shade light, airy lifestyle scenes.
records.poor_fit: Warm low-sun scenes, hard contrast and dark low-key images.

records.name: Superia-like
records.character: Everyday consumer negative: punchy greens, slightly magenta-leaning shadows, candid and imperfect.
records.suits: Casual city, nature and daily-life scenes, overcast streets and greenery.
records.poor_fit: Polished studio portraits and images needing refined skin rendering.

records.look: Slide film with vivid saturation, strong greens and blues, pronounced contrast and very fine grain. Deep shadows and bright highlights. For landscape and nature in bright daylight.

records.name: Velvia-like
records.character: Intense slide landscape character: very saturated greens and blues, deep shadows, high contrast and little tolerance for error.
records.suits: Wide landscapes and nature in soft directional light.
records.poor_fit: People, where skin turns unnatural, and contrasty harsh-light scenes.

records.look: Extremely fine grain and near-clinical clarity. Balanced contrast over a wide tonal range, with smooth transitions and detail at both ends. For studio, architecture and landscape in good light.
Strong contrast, deep blacks and visible grain that belongs to the image. Raw and atmospheric. For night, concerts and documentary, and usually pushed; the look depends on how far.
Modern fine grain, strong sharpness and a wide tonal range, with a clean contemporary feel and balanced contrast. For street, portraits and low light.
Balanced contrast, deep blacks and clear highlights, with grain more evident than fine-grain films, giving a raw documentary feel. Responds to push processing. For street, reportage and portraits.

records.name: HP5-like
records.character: Flexible black-and-white: moderate contrast, soft midtones, visible but gentle grain, wide latitude.
records.suits: Documentary, available-light portraits, quiet or overcast scenes.
records.poor_fit: Images whose meaning depends on colour relationships.

records.look: Bold and experimental, with strong contrast and pronounced grain. Reds, greens and blues can run intense or off neutral, and shifts depend on light and exposure. Imperfection is the point. Wants good light.

records.name: HARMAN Phoenix 200
records.notes: First-generation stock. Cannot render hues from blue through magenta to red: those fall to oranges of varying brightness. Dark, saturated blues and rich, varied greens. High contrast, low dynamic range, coarse grain and halation. Reported about 16% below reference saturation, and among the least accurate.

records.look: Strong contrast, pronounced grain and an unconventional palette that moves with the light. Reds and greens run intense while other tones stay restrained. Expressive rather than polished, with more dynamic range claimed than the first Phoenix.
Deliberately unnatural: deep reds, burnt oranges, muted yellows and an occasional eerie green. High contrast and noticeable grain, graphic and stylised. Wants bright, controlled light.

Black-and-white developed in the C-41 colour process. Smooth transitions, fine grain and fairly soft contrast, with highlights well held and shadows controlled. For everyday scenes, portraits and travel.
Fine grain, good sharpness, balanced contrast and a clean tonal range, in a classic monochrome manner. For portraits and landscape in bright light.

records.name: Kodachrome-like
records.character: Classic slide character: dense saturated reds and yellows, deep shadows, strong contrast, a mid-century documentary feel.
records.suits: Hard or bright daylight, street and travel with primary colours.
records.poor_fit: Low-key, low-contrast or pastel scenes, and deep shade.

records.look: Definite warmth and a yellow cast, with less detail than Gold. Good in bright outdoor light and too slow for evening or indoors. Underexposure shifts colour in the shadows.

records.name: Kodak ColorPlus 200
records.notes: Blues and golds are most saturated. Blues and cyans stay faithful, while reds and especially greens are compressed toward gold or orange, so skin leans orange. Ranked near the top for saturation, with an unsigned figure of about 8%.

records.look: Slide film that is clean, slightly cool and neutral, favouring realism. Crisp blues, clean whites, defined but not harsh contrast and extremely fine grain. For controlled daylight, landscape, travel and editorial.

Slide film, more neutral than colour negatives but less so than Provia, with a slight blue emphasis. Strong saturation and contrast, rich but not cartoonish. Little exposure latitude, so it rewards controlled light and slow work.
Vivid, with intense reds, blues and greens, and a polished, almost commercial clarity. Strong contrast, extremely fine grain, high sharpness. For daylight, landscape and travel.

Fine grain and very vibrant colour reminiscent of Kodachrome. Strongest in bright, colourful daylight, and needs correction in overcast or low light. Emphasises reds, so poor for portraits. Narrower latitude than Portra 400 or UltraMax, with colour shifting on slight exposure errors.

records.name: Kodak Ektar 100
records.palette: Two opposing axes led by blue, against golds and reds
records.notes: Evenly desaturated with high colour accuracy. Blues lean slightly cyan, greens slightly yellow, and reds toward orange, which turns skin orange. Purples and magentas go pastel. Fine grain and wide dynamic range.

records.name: Ektar-like
records.character: Vivid, fine-grained colour negative: saturated reds and blues, clean structure, relatively high colour contrast.
records.suits: Landscapes, travel and architecture with strong colour in good daylight.
records.poor_fit: Close portraits, where it pushes skin toward red.

records.look: Warm, richly saturated and nostalgic, with sun-warmed skin. At its best in daylight, for travel, portraits and everyday outdoor scenes. Camera, lens, exposure, light and scanning all change the result.
Balanced grain, sharp without being clinical, vibrant without being gaudy, slightly more saturated than the professional films. Narrower latitude than those films, so it suits daylight.

records.name: Kodak Gold 200
records.notes: A slightly warmer ColorPlus: reds more orange, greens less yellow but still leaning that way, reddened highlights, and weak magentas and violets. Suits vegetation and landscapes.

records.name: Gold-like
records.character: Warm consumer colour negative: golden yellows, nostalgic daylight, slightly rough and casual.
records.suits: Sunny snapshots, golden hour, family and travel memories.
records.poor_fit: Cool or moody scenes, night, and images relying on clean neutrals.

records.look: Neutral with gentle warmth, soft transitions, and neither contrast nor saturation pushed. Ultra-fine grain, with careful, accurate skin. Wants good light.
A subtle, gentle palette that favours depth over saturation, with fine grain. For portraits and weddings; its low speed makes it less versatile.

records.name: Kodak Portra 160
records.palette: Multipolar and balanced, with no dominant axis
records.notes: Very faithful hues, with greens clustered between green and yellow and purples toward blue. Soft to moderate desaturation apart from navy blue. Excellent skin. Very fine grain; little imposed personality.

records.look: Soft and neutral with slight warmth, flattering skin and fine, unobtrusive grain. For portraits, fashion, studio and everyday scenes, in natural or artificial light.

Balanced colour and very fine grain for a 400 film. Exceptionally wide latitude, especially towards overexposure, which makes it versatile in bright, dim and high-contrast scenes. So common that the writer calls it a cliché.

records.name: Kodak Portra 400
records.notes: Excellent fidelity, with greens slightly toward yellow and reds toward orange. Even desaturation, reported about 18% below reference, with only blue standing out. Strong magentas, violets and skin. Smooth for its speed; leaves the final look to the photographer.

records.name: Portra-like
records.character: Restrained warm negative: natural skin, gentle contrast, long highlight roll-off, understated saturation.
records.suits: Portraits and people in soft ambient light where skin is central.
records.poor_fit: Images without people that need punch, night or neon scenes, monochrome intent, and vivid landscapes.

records.look: Natural with gentle warmth and soft, controlled contrast. Wide latitude keeps detail at both ends. Grain is more visible than slower Portra but stays fine, and skin holds in difficult light. For low, mixed and indoor light.
Grainier and slightly more contrasty than Portra 400, with a more traditional look. Good for dim, moody scenes. Underexposure turns shadows green.
Saturated and contrasty, but grainier and less sharp than Ektar. A budget way into slow film; the writer disputes its use as a professional portrait film.

records.name: Kodak Pro Image 100
records.palette: Not established; the author doubts this roll
records.notes: Treat with caution: the author suspects an exposure or development problem. Washed-out result, with blues toward cyan, greens toward yellow and reds slightly orange. Grain is more visible than its speed suggests.

records.look: Rich midtones, very fine grain, excellent latitude, very sharp and detailed. For fine art and studio work.
Strong contrast, deep blacks and clear highlights, with controlled tonal structure for a fast film. Pronounced grain belongs to the image. For night, events and documentary, and pushed when needed.

Made to be pushed. Grain is far more prominent than other T-Max but controlled, and midtones lean to a middle grey rather than the usual pushed contrast, which some find flat. For low light, too grainy for detailed daylight work.
Like T-Max 100 with slightly more grain. Rich midtones and excellent latitude, versatile in almost any light.

Rich contrast, deep blacks and expressive grain, raw and classic. Highlights hold detail while shadows fall into strong, defined tones. For documentary, photojournalism and street, from daylight to low light.
Fine texture with slight grit at box speed and gradual midtone gradation. Pushing enlarges grain and raises contrast into a gritty look.

records.name: Tri-X-like
records.character: Gritty black-and-white: strong contrast, bold grain, deep blacks and graphic tonal structure.
records.suits: Street, reportage, hard light, strong shapes and expressive faces.
records.poor_fit: Delicate tonal scenes and images whose meaning depends on colour.

records.look: Vibrant and warm, with strong contrast, sharp rendering and slightly pronounced grain. For travel and everyday scenes, from daylight to lower light.
More pronounced grain that the writer finds pleasing, with colour more balanced than Gold, though not everyone likes either. Suits golden hour, and low light with a steady hand.

records.name: Kodak UltraMax 400
records.palette: Multipolar, with a slight blue to gold lean
records.notes: Named most accurate in this test, and most saturated, with blues and cyans beyond reference. The narration says +7.15%, though its ranking graphic is unsigned. Violets lean slightly blue. Medium, soft grain, and handles skin well.

records.name: LomoChrome Color 92
records.palette: Split-complementary, uniform blues against warm tones
records.notes: Saturated, uniform blues, with most other colours muted: faithful greens, yellows and reds slightly orange, cool violets and magentas. Reported about 21% below reference, the lowest here. Coarse grain and a painterly softness.

records.look: Deliberately muted, desaturated and slightly cool. Soft contrast with deep shadows, and present but controlled grain. Documentary and atmospheric, in varied light.
Extreme colour shift: greens become purples and magentas, while skin and blues can move unpredictably. Surreal, with moderate contrast and textured grain. The change is strongest in bright daylight.

records.name: Lomography Color Negative 400
records.notes: Highly saturated, with greens toward yellow and reds slightly toward orange. Greens and reds are held back compared with UltraMax, so the common claim that they are the same stock is not supported here. Skin leans slightly orange.

records.look: Moderate, controlled contrast with clear separation of blacks, whites and midtones. Fine, smooth grain and good sharpness. Wants bright daylight.
Stronger contrast and deeper blacks than the 100, with more pronounced grain, while keeping detail at both ends. For street, documentary and everyday scenes.

records.name: Monochrome
records.description: Neutral black-and-white rendering; optional yellow, red and green filters.

records.name: Film Onehundred 100
records.palette: Split-complementary, with dominant reds against cool greens and blues
records.notes: Yellows, golds and olive greens are desaturated, pure greens are boosted and pushed toward cyan, and reds stay strong with a slight magenta lean. Rich magentas and violets. Skin can go pink.

records.name: PRO Neg.Hi
records.description: Stronger tonal separation than PRO Neg.Std.

records.name: PRO Neg.Std
records.description: Low contrast portrait rendering intended for controlled light.

records.name: PROVIA/Standard
records.description: Balanced general-purpose colour with moderate contrast.

records.name: Velvia/Vivid
records.description: Emphasizes colour and contrast, especially landscape greens and reds.
